actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

device.name: Digit v3 box tower of Hanoi (MuJoCo model)

facts.text: The card's first model is the MJCF scene digit-v3-box-tower-of-hanoi.xml, whose root element is <mujoco model='digit'>
The model integrates with timestep 0.0005 s, Newton solver, 50 iterations, impratio 20, elliptic cone and gravity 0 0 -9.80665
The floating base of the torso is three slide joints (x, y and z, the z joint with ref 1.01) and a ball joint
The scene adds three box bodies (box0, box1 and box2), each with three slide joints and a ball joint

The actuator section has 20 motor actuators, one per named leg and arm joint, with per-motor ctrlrange: hip-roll, shoulder-roll, shoulder-pitch and elbow -1.4125 to 1.4125; hip-yaw and shoulder-yaw -1.5835307242068533 to 1.5835307242068533; hip-pitch -13.557993638726353 to 13.557993638726353; knee -14.457309387714753 to 14.457309387714753; toe-a and toe-b -0.8395188473154137 to 0.8395188473154137
The joint tree gives 82 qpos and 72 qvel coordinates: the base 3 slides and 1 ball, the three boxes 9 slides and 3 balls, and 30 hinges plus 6 balls in the legs and arms
The equality section has six connect constraints coupling the left and right achilles rods, toe-a rods and toe-b rods
The model has a gyro, an accelerometer and a magnetometer on the torso IMU site, with cutoff 34.9, 157 and 2.5 and noise 0.00173, 0.0396 and 0.001
The upstream evaluation entry point defaults --robot to "digit", with "h1" and "g1" as the other choices
The README names the Digit humanoid robot as the default robot

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state; the bridge takes no seed input and a reset restores the model defaults, so a run repeats exactly on the same engine but no seed selects a different one

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the model file for the actuator control ranges and the joint dimensions but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control target, so trajectories, contacts and actuator dynamics are not MuJoCo's

no mesh or texture of the stl asset directory is loaded and no contact, equality or tendon constraint is resolved by the stand-in; the six connect constraints of the model and the three box bodies are not simulated
the gyro, accelerometer and magnetometer of the model are not simulated, so no sensor or noise model contributes to the state
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
snapshot and restore use the bridge's fallback copy of time, qpos, qvel and ctrl, not MuJoCo's full integration state, because the stand-in has no mj_getState or mj_setState
no physical Digit robot is modelled and nothing was validated against the hardware
the package serves the card's first model only; the g1 and h1 MJCF scenes are separate models

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
